rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the eight-peak elution window while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. This establishes the critical pairs and a moderate-temperature baseline for subsequent slope and selectivity tests.

Double the gradient duration without changing the solvent endpoints or temperature to test which crowded pairs respond to slope. The initial last peak at 5.49 min suggests this shallower gradient can improve separation without a large time penalty.
The shallower gradient resolved all but one pair. Raise temperature while retaining the same gradient to test selectivity at that remaining near-coelution and shorten retention.

Back off temperature by one step to move away from the new late-pair near-coelution at 60 C. The remaining pairs have sufficient separation to make this a promising route to full resolution below 10 minutes.

Return to the best temperature and slightly steepen the gradient to shift the remaining critical pair while shortening the run. This also tests whether the marginally resolved earlier pair retains adequate separation.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step to fine-tune selectivity and slightly reduce gradient steepness around the nearly fully resolved method. This tests whether the R = 1.46 pair can reach baseline resolution without sacrificing the neighboring critical pairs.

Slightly reduce the gradient slope from injection 6 to improve the two early marginal pairs, using the late critical pair’s R = 1.78 as a buffer. The final organic fraction remains comfortably above the observed elution window.

Use a gradient slope of 0.045 organic fraction per minute, just steeper than injection 7, to lift the R = 1.49 pair while preserving the early pairs’ resolution. The narrower window achieves this fine slope adjustment on the grid and still ends above the last peak’s elution composition.

Injection 8 reaches the maximum CRF and remains the benchmark. Raise the starting organic fraction one step to seek a shorter fully resolved run, with the resulting shallower slope potentially offsetting compression of the early pairs.

Keep injection 8 as the maximum-score benchmark and explore a cooler selectivity regime with a steeper gradient. A substantial temperature change may separate the crowded compounds in a different order, opening a route to a faster fully resolved method.

Steepen the 25 C gradient to test whether the near-coeluting middle pair separates on the faster side of its selectivity crossover. This isolates the slope effect and seeks a shorter fully resolved alternative while retaining injection 8 as the maximum-score benchmark.

Test a higher starting organic fraction and a modest temperature increase to shift the two unresolved pairs in the fast, cool-temperature regime. Injection 8 remains the fully resolved benchmark while this run explores a potentially shorter alternative.

Test a steeper gradient at 25 C to move the unresolved middle pair farther from its apparent crossover and shorten the run. Monitor the neighboring middle pair and late pair for loss of resolution; injection 8 remains the maximum-score benchmark.

Explore the shallower-gradient side of the middle-pair crossover at 25 C, where the late pair should also gain resolution. Raising the starting organic fraction offsets the longer retention expected from the shallower slope, while injection 8 remains the maximum-score benchmark.

Keep injection 14’s gradient fixed and raise temperature to shift its single unresolved pair while shortening retention. This isolates temperature selectivity in the higher-starting-organic regime; injection 8 remains the maximum-score benchmark.

Test a substantially shallower gradient at 25 C to move beyond the middle-pair crossover seen in injection 14. A higher starting organic fraction should offset some added retention, potentially yielding a fully resolved alternative faster than injection 8.

Raise temperature one step while holding injection 16’s gradient fixed to shift its sole unresolved pair. The other pairs have substantial resolution margins, making this a promising test for full resolution with a shorter last-peak time.

Return to the fully resolved regime of injection 8 and increase gradient slope only slightly, from 0.045 to 0.04583 per minute. This tests whether retention can be shortened while keeping the two marginal early pairs at R ≥ 1.5.

Revisit the faster, higher-starting-organic method from injection 9 with a shallower slope to improve its unresolved early pair. This tests whether that pair can reach R ≥ 1.5 before the late pair loses its resolution margin, while retaining injection 8 as the maximum-score benchmark.

Trim the successful gradient window and shorten its programmed duration to eight minutes, with the endpoint still above the observed last-peak elution composition. This tests whether the slightly shallower slope preserves full resolution; injection 8 remains the maximum-score benchmark.

Explore a shallower gradient beyond the late-pair crossover, where separation may recover after elution-order reversal. The higher starting organic fraction limits retention time; injection 8 remains the established maximum-score method.

Test temperature selectivity at the narrower-window method from injection 19, seeking to separate its two critical pairs without excessive retention. Injection 8 already achieves the maximum CRF and remains the benchmark.

Revisit the 40 C regime with a shallower slope than injection 2 to separate its sole near-coeluting pair. Raising the starting organic fraction should offset some added retention and may keep a fully resolved alternative below 10 minutes; injection 8 remains the maximum-score benchmark.

Lower temperature one step from injection 23 to shift its sole unresolved pair, which has responded little to gradient-slope changes. This tests a nearby selectivity alternative, while injection 8 remains the established maximum-score method.

Use the final injection to slightly flatten injection 5’s gradient, targeting its R = 1.46 pair while checking that the late pair remains resolved. Injection 8 already achieves the maximum CRF and remains the recommended method unless this alternative also fully resolves all eight compounds.
